dedupe_keys.name: isimip data repository inter sectoral impact model intercomparison project

description: ISIMIP provides a framework and a public repository for consistently projecting the impacts of climate change across sectors, including water, agriculture, energy, lakes, coastal systems, fire, health and infrastructure, under common climate and socioeconomic scenarios. The project is coordinated from the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) with an international network of impact modellers. The repository at data.isimip.org holds the bias-adjusted climate forcing, socioeconomic input data (population, land use, dams, GDP) and the output of sector impact models for the simulation rounds ISIMIP2a, 2b, 3a, 3b and the new 4a and 4b; the home page counts 96, 88, 75 and 66 output datasets for rounds 2a to 3b, and ISIMIP4 started with the first CMIP7-based forcing. Files are global gridded netCDF, typically at 0.5 degree, searchable by simulation round, sector, model, variable and scenario, and downloadable free of charge after accepting the terms of use, under which each dataset carries its own licence. Caveats: outputs change between versions (a changelog must be checked), models differ strongly, and resolution is coarse for asset-level work. It supports scenario and climate adaptation analysis, hazard exposure of infrastructure under future river flooding, drought and heat, and multi-sector resilience studies, and supplies forcing used by models such as CLIMADA.
